name: Music
description: Songs, artists and the records they made.
theme: popular music from the twentieth century to now: the songs everyone can hum, the acts behind them, the albums that mattered, the instruments they were played on, and the handful of theory terms every listener has heard
angles: the act behind a song everyone can hum
the real name behind a stage name
which album a famous track sits on
the decade a landmark album or single arrived
acts known for one song, and the song
band line-ups, who played what, and who walked out
the writer of a song someone else made famous
cover versions, and who recorded it first
what a genre name actually means and where it started
a lyric quoted plainly, name the song
the song that opens or closes a famous film
duets and collaborations, who sang with whom
the nickname or honorific an artist is known by
the number an instrument is built around, its strings, keys, valves or pedals
the family an instrument belongs to, including the ones that surprise people
the instrument a famous riff or solo was played on
the name of a part of an instrument, the bridge, the reed, the fret, the bow
who invented an instrument, and roughly when
the Italian word written on a score, and what it tells the player to do
what a term every listener has heard actually means, tempo, key, octave, crescendo
the number behind the notation, beats in a bar, lines on a stave, semitones in an octave
two musical terms listeners routinely mix up, and which is which
avoid: current charts and streaming numbers, anything released in the last two years, celebrity personal lives, chart positions that differ from one country to the next, theory beyond what a keen listener would know, anything needing a score or an instrument in front of you, and questions where a cover version and the original would both be right
